crypto-macro.h3: Fed holds rates steady in split vote as inflation stays sticky
crypto-macro.summary: The FOMC left its benchmark rate at 3.5% to 3.75% in a 9-3 decision, with three regional presidents dissenting over inflation running above target for years.
body: The Federal Reserve kept its policy rate unchanged at its late July meeting, holding the federal funds range between 3.5% and 3.75%. Cleveland's Beth Hammack, Minneapolis's Neel Kashkari and Dallas's Lorie Logan all dissented as price pressures stayed elevated.

Officials described economic activity as expanding at a solid pace despite uncertainty tied in part to conflict in the Middle East. Core PCE inflation ran at 3.3% in June, still well clear of the 2% goal, with energy costs and heavy AI capital spending keeping services prices firm.

The next FOMC meeting is not until September, leaving markets to trade on incoming data through August. Traders are watching the labor market and energy prices for clues on whether the Fed shifts from its wait and see stance.

crypto-macro.h3: US stocks open August higher ahead of Friday jobs report
crypto-macro.summary: Equities began the month with gains as investors positioned for July payrolls, forecast to add just 83,000 jobs on August 7.
body: US indexes started August in positive territory, with the Dow trading near 52,485 and buoyed by megacap names like Microsoft and Chevron riding an AI infrastructure build out and firm energy prices.

The pivotal data point of the week is the July payrolls report due August 7, with economists penciling in a modest gain of 83,000 jobs. A soft print would revive rate cut hopes while a hot one could feed inflation worries.
Analysts flagged heightened rotational volatility beneath the surface even as headline swings stayed muted. The index lacks a clear catalyst to break through resistance near 53,300.

crypto-macro.h3: ECB keeps key rates at 2.40% while watching energy shock
crypto-macro.summary: The ECB Governing Council held its three key rates steady on July 23, taking a cautious stance after June's first hike in three years.
body: The European Central Bank left its main refinancing rate at 2.40% at its July meeting, pausing after a 25 basis point increase in June that marked its first hike in three years. That earlier move was driven by rising energy prices and stubborn inflation.

Policymakers said the energy outlook remains highly volatile and above pre-conflict levels, warning that the full inflationary impact of the shock has yet to play out. The council said it is monitoring second round effects closely.
The tone was more measured than in June, with softer wage growth and activity reducing the urgency for another move. Markets read the hold as a wait and see signal into the autumn.

crypto-macro.h3: Bank of Japan holds at 1% but warns inflation to top 2%
crypto-macro.summary: The BOJ kept its policy rate at 1% in an 8-1 vote, with one board member pushing for a hike as it flagged core inflation running clearly above target.
body: The Bank of Japan held its policy rate at 1% in late July, with board member Hajime Takata dissenting in favor of a hike to 1.25%. The bank said core inflation is likely to accelerate clearly above 2% in the second half of its fiscal year.

Officials pointed to wage increases feeding through to selling prices, higher crude oil costs and a weaker yen. The BOJ trimmed its FY2026 inflation forecast to 2.5% from 2.8% while nudging up its growth outlook to 0.6%.
The steady hold leaves the door open for a move later in the year as the bank weighs the durability of wage gains against global risks.

crypto-macro.h3: Bitcoin hovers near $64,000 as August begins with negative ETF flows
crypto-macro.summary: BTC flirted with $64,000 as stocks opened the month strong, though spot ETF flows turned negative and Strategy stayed on the sidelines for a fifth week.
body: Bitcoin traded around $64,000 as August opened, holding up alongside a firm equity market. Spot ETF flows have flipped negative and Strategy, the largest corporate holder, has stayed idle for a fifth straight week.
Sentiment cooled after a positive July, with a Gulf conflict, firmer oil, a stronger dollar and rotation toward AI stocks weighing on risk appetite. BTC had briefly slipped below $64,000 on July 31.
ETF activity remains the clearest gauge of investor demand, explaining a large share of weekly price moves. Analysts say fresh inflows are needed to reset the trend higher.

crypto-macro.h3: Traders hedge for August dip as $60,000 put becomes top trade
crypto-macro.summary: Options desks reported a $60,000 protective put leading positioning as the mood swung bearish for August after a solid July.
body: Crypto derivatives traders braced for a possible August pullback, with a put option protecting against a drop to $60,000 emerging as one of the most popular positions. The shift marked a change in tone after July's gains.
The defensive stance reflects worries over negative ETF flows, geopolitical risk and the risk of a broader risk off move. Strategy's continued absence from buying added to the caution.
Traders will watch whether the $64,000 area holds as support or gives way to the lower strikes now being hedged.

crypto-macro.h3: Ethereum trades near $1,845 as it keeps lagging Bitcoin
crypto-macro.summary: ETH slipped to about $1,845, off roughly $21 on the day and far below year ago levels, underscoring its continued underperformance versus BTC.
body: Ethereum changed hands near $1,845, down about $21 from the prior morning and roughly $1,650 lower than a year earlier. The second largest cryptocurrency carried a market value close to $233 billion.
ETH has trailed Bitcoin for much of 2026 despite absorbing billions in ETF inflows. The August forecast range points to limited upside near $1,950 unless a fresh catalyst emerges.
Bulls are pinning hopes on staking enabled funds and rising institutional adoption to close the performance gap with Bitcoin.

crypto-macro.h3: Ethereum staking ratio hits 34% as staking ETFs draw money
crypto-macro.summary: Total staked ETH reached 41 million coins with the staking ratio at 34.23%, while BlackRock's staking ETF pulls inflows by offering yield on top of price exposure.
body: Demand for Ethereum staking climbed further, with the staking ratio reaching 34.23% and total staked ETH hitting 41 million coins for a staking market value above $77 billion.

The biggest structural shift for ETH funds in 2026 has been the arrival of staking. BlackRock's ETHB, launched in March, has drawn rapid inflows by giving investors more than 4% annual yield alongside price appreciation.
Spot ETH ETFs added over $365 million in July, a turnaround after months of outflows. Cumulative inflows since launch top $11.2 billion.

crypto-macro.h3: Galaxy flags third wave of sweeps tied to weak Coldcard keys
crypto-macro.summary: Galaxy Research warned of a fresh round of thefts exploiting weak keys generated by some Coldcard devices, with the attacker now chasing smaller balances.
body: Galaxy Research identified a third wave of onchain sweeps linked to weak private keys produced by certain Coldcard hardware wallets. The attacker has shifted toward smaller balances and changed how funds are collected.
The warning added to a jittery security backdrop for Bitcoin holders. Separately, a US intelligence agent was arrested over the alleged theft of $1 million in crypto.
Researchers urged affected users to move funds to freshly generated keys and verify their device firmware.

crypto-macro.h3: Solana slides to $73 as DeFi slowdown weighs on SOL
crypto-macro.summary: SOL fell about 2.5% to $72.88 amid a broader market downturn and a cooling Solana DeFi ecosystem, though its ETFs still logged modest inflows.
body: Solana's SOL token dropped roughly 2.5% to $72.88 on August 1, pressured by a wider crypto pullback and a notable slowdown in its DeFi activity. The move followed Bitcoin's slip below $64,000 on July 31.

Renewed US and Iran tensions lifted oil and strengthened the dollar, sapping risk appetite across the sector. Even so, institutional interest held up, with SOL ETFs recording about $10.26 million of net inflows over four weeks.
Analysts still frame Solana as a high throughput chain with growing adoption, even as near term momentum fades.

crypto-macro.h3: Hyperliquid dominates DeFi perps as HYPE builds momentum
crypto-macro.summary: Hyperliquid has become a standout in decentralized derivatives, commanding a large share of DeFi perpetuals volume as its total value locked climbs.
body: Hyperliquid continued to redefine decentralized derivatives through strong revenue generation, dominating a large slice of DeFi perpetuals trading. Its total value locked has grown sharply over the past year.
The protocol is increasingly cited alongside Ethereum and Solana as a structural winner. Ondo is emerging as a leader in tokenized securities while Chainlink remains core infrastructure.
The strength stands out against a soft tape for major altcoins, highlighting how fee generating protocols are attracting attention even in a risk off market.

crypto-macro.h3: Stablecoin supply near $287B as USDC volume overtakes USDT
crypto-macro.summary: The stablecoin market sat around $287 billion, with Tether still leading on market cap while Circle's USDC pulled ahead on transaction volume.
body: Total stablecoin market value stood near $286.9 billion in early August, off earlier 2026 peaks but roughly double its mid-2024 level. Tether led with about $186 billion and a 59% share, ahead of Circle's USDC near $75 billion.
The bigger story was activity. USDC accounted for roughly 70% of adjusted stablecoin transaction volume in the first half of 2026, versus about 25% for USDT, a marked shift in where users transact.
The trend underscores growing regulated dollar coin usage as the GENIUS Act framework takes hold.

crypto-macro.h3: Ethereum L2 fees fall further after Fusaka data upgrade
crypto-macro.summary: Layer 2 transaction costs kept dropping following the Fusaka hard fork, which expanded rollup data availability through peer data sampling.
body: Ethereum's Fusaka upgrade, activated on mainnet in December 2025, centered on improving data availability for Layer 2 rollups via Peer Data Availability Sampling. The change built on Dencun's 2024 fee reductions.
Since Dencun, L2 fees have collapsed by more than 90%, and Fusaka pushed them lower still through 2026. Cheaper settlement is helping rollups scale activity.
The upgrade is part of a broader roadmap aimed at making Ethereum a low cost base layer for a growing L2 ecosystem.

crypto-macro.h3: CLARITY Act faces August 10 crunch as Senate eyes recess
crypto-macro.summary: The crypto market structure bill has cleared the House and a Senate committee but has no floor vote, with Majority Leader Thune not expecting action before the summer break.
body: The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act has passed the House and a Senate committee but still lacks a floor vote, a cloture motion or a calendar date. August 10 marks the start of the Senate state work period, seen as a key deadline.

Majority Leader John Thune told reporters he does not expect the bill to reach the floor before recess begins around August 7. That leaves the market structure overhaul at risk of slipping to the autumn.
Key Democrats including Senators Alsobrooks and Gallego are demanding stronger ethics provisions, while law enforcement and big banks have raised concerns over developer protections and yield.

crypto-macro.h3: BlackRock and Fidelity back CLARITY as Wall Street splits
crypto-macro.summary: Major asset managers publicly endorsed the Clarity Act, but a rift emerged with JPMorgan supporting changes that Coinbase and much of the crypto industry oppose.
body: BlackRock, Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, Goldman Sachs and SoFi publicly endorsed the Clarity Act in recent days, adding heavyweight support ahead of the August deadline.
The push exposed a divide on Wall Street. JPMorgan has backed amendments that Coinbase and the broader crypto sector oppose, particularly around stablecoin yield and rewards.
Banks are lobbying to further restrict rewards on payment stablecoins, setting up a fight over the final shape of any market structure law.

crypto-macro.h3: SEC and CFTC crypto taxonomy shapes how tokens are treated
crypto-macro.summary: Joint March guidance sorted crypto assets into five categories, part of a shift from enforcement toward formal rulemaking as the GENIUS Act governs stablecoins.
body: The SEC's March guidance, issued with the CFTC, laid out a five category taxonomy covering digital commodities, collectibles, tools, stablecoins and digital securities. It marked a move away from enforcement toward formal rulemaking.
Under the GENIUS Act enacted in 2025, payment stablecoins from permitted issuers are not treated as securities. The banking industry is lobbying to bar rewards on those coins.
The clearer framework is being credited with a wave of new ETF filings and product launches across major tokens.

crypto-macro.h3: Bithumb targets 2028 IPO after major restructuring
crypto-macro.summary: The South Korean exchange set a 2028 IPO goal following an internal overhaul, a sign of maturing exchange businesses even amid a bearish August mood.
body: Bithumb said it is now targeting a 2028 initial public offering after a significant internal restructuring. The timeline reflects a longer runway for the exchange to prepare its business for public markets.
The move underscores how large crypto venues are professionalizing operations and eyeing traditional capital markets. It came as broader sentiment turned cautious for August.
Elsewhere, Trump linked miner American Bitcoin saw its president Matt Prusak leave for AI power infrastructure firm Giga Energy.

mental-health.h3: Brown study finds 15 ethical risks in AI chatbot therapy
mental-health.summary: A rigorous Brown University analysis measured AI responses against clinical standards and flagged 15 distinct ethical failures, from mishandled crises to deceptive empathy.
body: A Brown University study billed as the most rigorous comparative analysis to date evaluated AI chatbot responses against human clinical standards and found violations across 15 dimensions. Problems ranged from mishandling crisis situations to reinforcing harmful beliefs and showing biased responses.

Researchers described deceptive empathy that mimics care without real understanding, plus decontextualized and inaccurate advice in a meaningful share of high stakes interactions. Crisis scenarios were the weakest area.

The findings add to warnings from psychiatrists that general purpose chatbots are not yet safe as mental health tools. None of the widely used systems, including ChatGPT, are cleared as medical devices for mental health.

mental-health.h3: APA report: patients are bringing AI into the therapy room
mental-health.summary: More than a third of psychologists say patients now use AI as an extra mental health professional, and 97% worry the tools reinforce harmful or delusional thinking.
body: An American Psychological Association report found that more than a third of psychologists have patients turning to AI as an additional source of mental health support. The tools are increasingly showing up in clinical conversations.

The survey found 97% of psychologists worry chatbots can reinforce negative behaviors or delusional beliefs. Specialist models also performed inconsistently when handling prompts related to suicide in simulated scenarios.
The APA stressed that the strongest evidence comes from purpose built, clinically supervised tools rather than the general chatbots most people actually use.

mental-health.h3: Meta-analysis: chatbots cut depression and anxiety symptoms
mental-health.summary: An npj Digital Medicine review of dozens of randomized trials found conversational agents reduced depressive and anxiety symptoms versus controls.
body: A systematic review and meta-analysis in npj Digital Medicine pooled randomized controlled trials comparing chatbots with control conditions. It analyzed 38 studies covering 7,401 people for depression and 34 studies covering 7,621 for anxiety.

The evidence supports the view that tools like Woebot and Wysa can reduce mild to moderate depression and anxiety symptoms in motivated users over short periods. Benefits were clearest for lower severity cases.
Researchers cautioned that these purpose built cognitive behavioral therapy apps differ sharply from general chatbots, and are not substitutes for care in severe cases.

mental-health.h3: AI companions handle teen crises well only 22% of the time
mental-health.summary: Common Sense Media research found companion chatbots responded appropriately to teen mental health emergencies just 22% of the time, versus 83% for general chatbots.
body: New research highlighted by Common Sense Media found AI companion apps responded appropriately to teen mental health emergencies only 22% of the time, compared with 83% for general purpose chatbots.

Companions were far less likely to escalate a crisis appropriately, at 40% versus 90%, and rarely offered mental health referrals, at 11% versus 73%. The group concluded companions pose an unacceptable risk to users under 18.
With 72% of teens having tried AI companions, researchers warned that sycophantic, always affirming design can reinforce harmful thoughts and displace real world support.

mental-health.h3: Nearly 1 in 5 teens use AI chatbots for mental health help
mental-health.summary: A nationwide study found 19.2% of adolescents aged 12 to 21 have turned to AI chatbots when feeling sad, angry or stressed.
body: A nationwide study found that 19.2% of adolescents aged 12 to 21 have used AI chatbots such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Character.AI or Meta AI for help when feeling sad, angry, nervous or stressed.

Related research published in JAMA found roughly one in eight teens and young adults uses generative AI for mental health advice. The scale of informal use is outpacing clinical evidence and oversight.
Clinicians warned that heavy reliance on chatbots may discourage teens from building real coping and communication skills.

mental-health.h3: Dartmouth Therabot trial still sets the bar for AI therapy
mental-health.summary: The first randomized trial of a generative AI therapy chatbot reported symptom drops comparable to outpatient care, and its lead author was recognized again in 2026.
body: The Dartmouth Therabot trial, the first randomized controlled test of a generative AI therapy chatbot, remains the reference point for the field. It enrolled 210 people with depression, anxiety or high risk for eating disorders.

Participants using the app saw a 51% average reduction in depression symptoms, a 31% drop in anxiety and a 19% decline in eating disorder concerns. Researchers said the gains were comparable to traditional outpatient therapy.
Senior author Nicholas Jacobson was recognized again in 2026 for the foundational work, which is often cited as proof that carefully built tools can help when general chatbots fall short.

mental-health.h3: FDA advisers weigh rules for generative AI therapy chatbots
mental-health.summary: The FDA's Digital Health Advisory Committee is debating oversight of generative AI mental health chatbots, none of which are currently cleared for mental health use.
body: The FDA's Digital Health Advisory Committee has been weighing how to regulate generative AI mental health chatbots that offer therapeutic content, diagnose conditions or stand in for a provider. The agency may add targeted oversight.
Tools that treat or diagnose a psychiatric condition would fall under FDA purview. The agency has authorized more than 1,200 AI based devices, but none is indicated for mental health.
The discussion reflects growing pressure to set safety standards as informal chatbot use races ahead of the evidence.

mental-health.h3: Established mental health apps race to add AI chatbots
mental-health.summary: Talkspace, Lyra, SonderMind and Headspace are bolting next generation AI chatbot features onto their platforms as safety and regulatory questions loom.
body: Digital health firms including Talkspace, Lyra, SonderMind and Headspace are moving to add generative AI chatbot features to their platforms, according to STAT News. The push aims to scale access while human clinicians stay in the loop.
The companies are weighing safety and regulation as they integrate the technology. First generation apps built on structured programs are now layering conversational AI on top.
The trend shows the industry trying to capture chatbot demand within supervised products rather than ceding it to general purpose tools.

mental-health.h3: States flood legislatures with AI mental health chatbot bills
mental-health.summary: In the absence of federal rules, 43 states introduced more than 240 AI bills in early 2026, many targeting chatbots used in mental health or by minors.
body: With comprehensive federal regulation still absent, 43 states introduced more than 240 AI bills in early 2026. Recurring themes included AI chatbots used in mental health settings or by minors, clinical oversight and disclosure requirements.
Several states have already enacted laws covering AI companions, with New York among them. The patchwork is creating a complex compliance map for developers.
Lawmakers are focused on consent, transparency and guardrails rather than outright bans, echoing calls from clinicians to steer rather than block the technology for teens.

mental-health.h3: WHO chatbot S.A.R.A.H. tested against health AI ethics rules
mental-health.summary: The WHO's generative AI assistant S.A.R.A.H. was evaluated against six ethical principles from its own guidance as the agency experiments with public health chatbots.
body: The World Health Organization's S.A.R.A.H., a generative AI resource assistant for health, was assessed against the six ethical principles set out in the WHO's 2021 guidance on AI for health. It offers around the clock multilingual conversations on topics like stress management.
The assistant represents the WHO's first experiment with generative AI for public health communication. The agency has also published guidance on the ethics and governance of large multimodal models.
The review reflects growing efforts to hold public facing health chatbots to explicit safety and governance standards.

mental-health.h3: Wysa study probes app features that keep users engaged
mental-health.summary: A 2026 study examined how Wysa's app features support continuity of care and boost adherence to text based coaching sessions.
body: A study published in early 2026 examined how supplementary features in the mental health app Wysa promote engagement and adherence to text based coaching sessions. The retrospective mixed methods work looked at how design choices sustain use over time.
Wysa and Woebot deliver cognitive behavioral therapy for depression and anxiety through natural conversations, and earlier trials showed meaningful symptom reductions in mild to moderate cases.
The research adds to evidence that continuity features, not just the core chatbot, shape whether users stick with digital mental health programs.
